citations.cite: California Court of Appeal, Third Appellate District
citations.quote: The statute has since been amended to include protection for “reproductive health decisionmaking.” (See § 12940, subd. (a), as amended through Sen. Bill No. 523 (2021-2022 Reg. Sess.), effective Jan. 1, 2023.)
citations.case: Paleny v. Fireplace Products U.S., Inc. (Cal. Ct. App., Third Dist., filed June 27, 2024, certified for publication), footnote 3

citations.cite: California Court of Appeal, Third Appellate District
citations.quote: Appellant also does not address the retroactivity of this amendment other than to assert, in her reply brief, as she did at oral argument, that the amendment was a mere clarification of existing law, i.e., the forms of sex discrimination, and thus presents no question of retroactivity. As we have indicated, the issue of retroactivity was not addressed in her opening brief, and we thus find it forfeited.
citations.case: Paleny v. Fireplace Products U.S., Inc. (Cal. Ct. App., Third Dist., filed June 27, 2024, certified for publication)

citations.cite: California Court of Appeal, Third Appellate District
citations.quote: Again, there is no evidence that appellant was pregnant, infertile, or addressing some other medical condition. She was undergoing an elective medical procedure but, without an underlying medical condition related to pregnancy, appellant does not have a protected characteristic under the FEHA.
citations.case: Paleny v. Fireplace Products U.S., Inc. (Cal. Ct. App., Third Dist., filed June 27, 2024, certified for publication)
